ecopedia.summary: The Rabotnik Logbook is a Rabotnik's home base: place it to bring in a worker, and stock it to keep the worker going.
ecopedia.section:
The Rabotnik Logbook is crafted at a Carpentry Table with Carpentry level 1, from 20 Plant Fibers and 10 Wood Boards.
Place it inside a room of a house within a settlement. It can sit on tables, like a lamp. A Logbook outside a settlement still gets a Rabotnik, but the Rabotnik waits and does nothing until the Logbook is inside one.
Once a Rabotnik moves in, the Logbook is named after it, and its name is printed in gold on the spine. You can edit the spine text like a sign's, but the Rabotnik's name comes back on its next update.
Picking the Logbook up retires its Rabotnik. The Rabotnik moves out, leaves the settlement and keeps its savings. See [Rabotniks Overview].

The Logbook has 8 storage slots and accepts only what the Rabotnik uses: - Food, which the Rabotnik eats when it gets hungry. - Skill scrolls. The first one stocked becomes the Rabotnik's skill, if it has none yet. - Harvest tools: sickles and scythes for crops, and axes for trees. A Rabotnik needs these for [Rabotnik Contracts|Rabotnik Contracts] that involve harvesting. Chainsaws don't count.

- Rabotnik: the Rabotnik's name, skill and level, calories, supplies, and the nutrition and housing parts of its [Experience] rate. This tab also has the base skill buttons. - Home and Money: citizenship, home, rent, bank balance, and what the Rabotnik has earned and spent. Choose a currency and an amount, then press Fund Worker to send money from your own account to the Rabotnik. - Activity: what the Rabotnik did on its last update, its lifetime record (labor, meals, parties, items hauled, plants harvested, contracts), and an event log.

By default, the Logbook's owner gets a chat message when the Rabotnik's situation changes. For example, when it: - becomes a citizen, - moves in or loses its home, - learns its skill, - runs out of food, - runs low on rent money (fewer than 12 hours of rent left), or - joins a work party.
A Logbook counts as a Cultural furnishing, like a painting. Its value is the culture its Rabotnik creates, which grows with the Rabotnik's quality of life and reputation. See [Rabotniks in Society].
